subject.title: fix: protect SMS webhook callback quota [AI]

question: Is a 300-request-per-minute unauthenticated pre-validation allowance per resolved SMS account/route/client key an acceptable ingress boundary?
rationale: The separation fixes the quota-poisoning bug, but choosing how much unsigned parsing and signature work to permit is a security and availability tradeoff that repository history and unit tests cannot settle.

options.title: Prove and retain the split
options.body: Keep the two-stage design, establish the lowest operationally safe pre-validation threshold with live proxy evidence, and add an in-flight bound if load observations require one.

options.title: Accept 300 explicitly
options.body: Approve the proposed 300-request allowance as an intentional availability tradeoff and require only the missing real webhook proof before merge.

options.title: Pause the change
options.body: Hold the PR until production traffic requirements or an incident report justify increasing the unauthenticated ingress budget.

recommendation.title: Prove and retain the split
recommendation.body: Keep the two-stage design, establish the lowest operationally safe pre-validation threshold with live proxy evidence, and add an in-flight bound if load observations require one.

likelyOwner.reason: The SMS webhook and its original quota policy were introduced through this person's merged feature history.
